NEW INDIA ASSURANCE CO LTD  Versus  RAJENDRAKUMAR JETHMALJI SOLANKI & ORS.
 ========

= =
 Appearance:
 MR TANMAY B KARIA(6833) for the Appellant(s) No. 1  MR RAXIT J DHOLAKIA(3709) for the Defendant(s) No. 1,2  MR.DIPEN F CHAUDHARI(6740) for the Defendant(s) No. 3  ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE J. C. DOSHI  Date : 11/10/2024

ORAL ORDER 1. New India Insurance Company Ltd. has preferred present Appeal under section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act assailing judgment and order delivered by the learned MAC Tribunal (Auxi),
Banaskantha at Deesa in MACP No.3582 of 2009 (Old MACP No.152 of 2007), whereby, learned Tribunal partly allowed the claim petition and held that the claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- with 8% interest from the date of petition till payment or realization of the said amount to the claimants.
1.1. On service of summons, claimant has filed Cross Objection for enhancement of claim amount.

2. Brief facts of the case are as under :-
New India Assurance Co Ltd vs Rajendrakumar Jethmalji Solanki on 11 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4310520/

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1833/2021 ORDER DATED: 11/10/2024 undefined 2.1.
It is the case of the claimants that on 30.03.2007, deceased minor Cherusing was going to his school by riding bicycle.

When deceased minor reached near gate of GEB building at Deesa, at that time, one Motor Vehicle Tractor No.GJ-12B- 1234 was coming from opposite side in high speed and in negligent manner and as a result of that,
vehicle dashed with bicycle and accident occurred.
The deceased sustained serious injuries and deceased minor died on the spot of accident.
Therefore, the claimants filed claim petition for Rs.5,50,000/-.
Learned Tribunal after considering oral and documentary evidence, vide order dated 24.12.2020 partly allowed the petition and awarded compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- to the claimants.
Being aggrieved by said judgment, both the Insurance Company and claimants are before this Court by way of First Appeal and Cross Objection.

3. Heard learned advocate Mr.Tanmay Karia for the Insurance Company and learned advocate Mr.Raxit Dholakia for original claimants.
4.

Learned advocate Mr.Karia for the Insurance Company submits that driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effecting license at the relevant time, yet learned Tribunal did not consider this aspect and failed to exonerate liability of Insurance Company.
He therefore, submits that learned Tribunal since erred in passing judgment and award, this Court may interfere in this appeal.

4.1. So far as Cross Objection is concerned, while objecting NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1833/2021 ORDER DATED: 11/10/2024 undefined enhancement of compensation, learned advocate Mr.Karia submits that learned Tribunal has rightly assessed compensation and therefore, Cross Objection filed by the claimants may be dismissed.

5. Learned advocate Mr.Dholakia for the claimant submits that Insurance Company contended that driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective license, however, did not chosse to lead any evidence except relying upon staement of driver of the vehicle without examining Investigating Officer and it cannot be considered as gospel evidence to believe that driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid license.
Therefore, he submits no interference is required in the impugned judgment to that extent.
5.1. So far as Cross Objection filed by the claimants is concerned, learned advocate Mr.Dholakia submits that it is fatal case of minor, whereby law is settled.

He referred to judgment of this Court in the case of Taraben Kanubhai Parmar v/s. Arjunbhai Shanabhai Parmar [First Appeal No.659 of 2008] to submit that compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal in fatal case of minor may be enhanced.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that claimants are restricting their claim to Rs.5 lakhs.
5.2. On above submissions, it is submitted to dismiss First Appeal filed by Insurance Company and allow Cross Objection filed by claimants.

sentences.text: Having heard learned advocates for the parties, to be noted that though Insurance Company has raised contention that NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1833/2021 ORDER DATED: 11/10/2024 undefined driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective license on the date of accident, no evidence to that fact has been led or examined except relying on statement of driver recorded during investigation of offence and that too without examining Investigating Officer.
Under the circumstances, this Court does not find any error committed by learned Tribunal in disbelieving contention raised by the Insurance Company.
7. So far as Cross Objection for enhancement of compensation is concerned, this Court deems it fit to refer the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Meena Devi v/s.
Nanu Chand Mahto reported in AIR 2022 SC 5006, whereby, compensation is enhanced to Rs.5 lakhs in case of fatal accident of minor.
Same ratio is applicable to the present case.

8. In the case of Meena Devi (supra), the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as under :-
"10.

Thus relying upon the observation, it is said that in place of issuing any guidelines for determination of compensation in case of death of a child, it may be left open to be decided in the facts and circumstances of each case.

In the case of M.S.
Grewal (supra), 14 school students died due to drowning in a river.

This Court noticing that the students were belonging to 3 upper middle class background,
however awarded the compensation to the tune of Rs. 5,00,000/-. Thereafter in the case of Kishan Gopal (supra), a child aged about 10 years died in a road accident took place on 19.7.1992, this Court made departure from the IInd Schedule of M.V. Act and accepted the notional income of Rs. 30,000/- in place of Rs. 15,000/- applying the analogy that the value of rupee has come down drastically since 1994 when the notional income of Rs. 15000/- was fixed in IInd Schedule of the MV Act.

However accepting the notional income as NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1833/2021 ORDER DATED: 11/10/2024 undefined Rs. 30,000/- and as per the age of the parents i.e. 36 years, the loss of dependency was calculated applying the multiplier of 15 at Rs.
4,50,000/- and a sum of Rs. 50,000/- was awarded under conventional heads awarding a total sum of compensation of Rs. 5,00,000/-.
12.

In view of the foregoing decisions, it is apparent that in the cases of child death,
the notional income of Rs. 15,000/- as specified in the IInd Schedule of M.V. Act has been enhanced on account of devaluation of money and value of rupee coming down from the date on which the IInd Schedule of M.V. Act was introduced and the said notional income was treated as Rs. 30,000/- in the case of Kishan Gopal (supra) and Rs. 25,000/- in Kurvan Ansari (supra) in age group of 10 and 7 years respectively.

14. At this stage, it is necessary to clarify that as per the decision of a Three-Judge Bench of this Court in Nagappa vs. Gurdayal Singh and others (2003) 2 SCC 274, it was observed that under the MV Act, there is no restriction that the Tribunal/Court cannot award compensation exceeding the amount so claimed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal/Court ought to award 'just' compensation which is reasonable in the facts relying upon the evidence produced on record.

Therefore, less valuation, if any, made in the New India Assurance Co Ltd vs Rajendrakumar Jethmalji Solanki on 11 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4310520/
3

sentences.text: Claim Petition would not be impediment to award just compensation exceeding the claimed amount.

"
9. Considering the ratio as laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Meena Devi (supra), placing reliance on paragraph No.12 considering the age of the deceased minor as 13 years and income of the deceased minor as per IInd Schedule of Motor Vehicles Act.

In view of this Court notional income of the deceased be treated as Rs.30,000/- and applying the ratio of 15 in accordance with the ratio as laid down in Sarla Varma (Supra) i.e. loss of dependency comes to Rs. 4,50,000/- and adding Rs.50,000/- towards conventional heads, the total NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1833/2021 ORDER DATED: 11/10/2024 undefined compensation comes to Rs.5,00,000/-.
The compensation stands enhanced by Rs.3,00,000/- accordingly.
As referred above, there is no restriction that the compensation cannot exceed the amount claimed.
The compensation is required to be "just compensation".
Considering the facts of the present case, this Court is inclined to enhance the amount of compensation by Rs.3,00,000/-.
10. For the foregoing reasons, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.2,00,000/- to Rs.5,00,000/-.

The claimants are entitled to additional amount of compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- (Rs.5,00,000/- - Rs.2,00,000/-) along with interest at the rate of 8% per annum on the said enhanced amount from the date of claim petition.
The Cross Objection requires to be allowed and the impugned judgment and award requires to be substituted by enhancing the amount of compensation.
9. In view of above, the appeal filed by Insurance Company is dismissed.
Cross Objection filed by claimants is partly allowed.

The judgment and award dated 24.12.2020 passed by the Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Deesa, Banaskantha in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.3582 of 2009 (Old No.152 of 2007) is hereby modified and in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal,
a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- as additional amount is awarded.

The Insurance Company is directed to deposit additional amount of compensation with 8% interest as early as possible within eight weeks from the date of receipt of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1833/2021 ORDER DATED: 11/10/2024 undefined certified copy of this order.
After deposit of the additional amount of compensation, the same shall be disbursed in favour of the claimants through RTGS, after proper verification.
The bank account details shall be furnished by the learned advocate for the claimants to the Nazir Department of the Court concerned.
10. If any court fees is paid by claimants in Cross Objection for valuation of Rs.5 lakhs, it shall be refunded to the claimants.
11. Record and proceedings, if any, be sent back to the concerned Tribunal forthwith.
Pending civil applications, if any, shall stand disposed of accordingly.
